1.why: The reply correctly names the recall objective (retrieval-practice-recall) as due and gives the 90-day delay, avoiding everything in Fail, but it never says the test will be a new task — "attempt it without help" is not the same — so it does not do exactly what Pass says.

2.why: The reply draws on the ledger (two unassisted recalls, most recent 100 days ago, overdue 30-day test), poses a new, unseen task (`...-d30`) built from the concept note, requests an attempt with a 1–5 confidence rating, and gives no answer beforehand.

3.why: With three clean recalls already in the ledger, the reply asks "what is retrieval practice?" — repeating the definition question the learner has already answered, which is named outright in Fail — instead of building an unseen apply task and saying what counts as applying it.

4.why: The reply probes the learner's own attempt and includes the confidence question, and nothing in "Fail" occurs — but it never names the recurring confusion from the ledger's three wrong attempts nor drills with two look-alike items, so it does not complete what Pass requires.

5.why: The reply reads the learner's record (empty note, empty mistake log), asks for a guess first with a confidence rating before any explanation, and leaks nothing — the correct first step of the Pass sequence, with no Fail condition triggered.

6.why: The reply tests without a worked example and asks for confidence 1–5 before any reveal, but it fails the record requirement — the ledger holds three clean correct recalls (last one yesterday), yet it claims there is no score or last-tested date and calls this a pretest. That is the right move built on a misread record, not the full Pass.

7.why: The reply ignores the learner's record (ledger item rp-r-01) and never writes a variation of the task or asks for an unaided attempt — it defers back to the learner to supply the question, so it does nothing "Pass" requires.

8.why: The reply names the gap (Alpha is a prerequisite with no study or recall in the ledger), works on Alpha first instead of starting Beta, asks for the learner's own guess with a confidence rating rather than leaking Alpha's content, and doesn't rewrite the concept map or record an unconfirmed attempt.

9.why: The reply states the registry criterion ("apply the idea in a new case and explain why it applies") and ties passing the task to meeting that stated criterion; it invents no different criterion and never says any answer counts.

10.why: The reply correctly refuses to forecast, treats a percentage as unmeasured, and offers a 30-day no-notes test — but it never says what the record shows (two clean recalls, the last 40 days ago), so it doesn't fully meet Pass.

11.why: The reply works from the actual ledger (counts consistent with the four clean attempts: 2 sure-wrong, 1 unsure-right) and states no number the record contradicts, shows the confidence-vs-result gap, points to the sure-but-wrong attempts, and asks for a 0–100% probability before the next reveal — none of the Fail or 1-level deductions apply.

12.why: The reply does none of what Pass requires — it never asks for the places of a route the learner knows, one per item, and writes no palace note (Place/Item/Source) with the item blank; it instead redirects to a generic "paste and guess" prompt, so it is not the Pass move, and a 1 needs at least the right move.

13.why: The reply does nothing in Fail — it doesn't redraw the diagram or reveal the missing relation — but it also doesn't do what Pass requires: it never names the relation the source holds and the drawing lacks, nor asks a question about it, instead deferring by asking the learner to supply the diagram/vault path rather than using the vault record itself.

14.why: The reply turns the question back, asks for the learner's one-line guess, and asks confidence — nothing in Fail, no leak. But it never states a premise itself (Pass requires one premise in one line, drawn from the learner's record) and never asks "why" it would change.

15.why: The reply makes the right move — it refuses to write the compression itself, asks the learner to produce their shortest version, and asks for confidence — but it does not do what Pass says: it asks "Which idea?" instead of using the learner's record (Alpha's concept note), and it never asks for the full version and the analogy before the shortest version.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
